topic: singular and plural nouns; a / an
rule_en: Use a/an before singular nouns: a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound. Use 'the' before singular or plural nouns to refer to something specific. Regular plurals add -s, -es (after ch, sh, s, ss, x), or change y to -ies after a consonant.
structure: a/an + singular noun; noun + s/es/ies for plural

rule_en: This/these refer to things near you; that/those refer to things that are not near you (there or over there). This/that are singular, these/those are plural. They can also be used for people.
structure: this/that + singular noun; these/those + plural noun

What are these? They're keys.
What's that? It's a cat.
This is my brother.

rule_en: Was/were is the past form of am/is/are. To make negatives, add n't (wasn't/weren't). There is/are becomes there was/there were in the past. Past time expressions like yesterday, last night, last week are commonly used.
structure: Subject + was/were (+not); Was/Were + subject...?
examples_en: I was at home at 8.00.
You were in class yesterday.
Was she a singer? Yes, she was. No, she wasn't.
There was a party at the school last night.

rule_en: The past simple is used to talk about the past and is the same for all persons. Regular verbs add -ed (or -d if the verb ends in e); a final consonant+y changes to -ied; a verb ending consonant-vowel-consonant doubles the final consonant before -ed. Use did (not do/does) to make questions and negatives.
structure: Subject + verb+ed; negative: didn't + infinitive; question: Did + subject + infinitive?
examples_en: I arrived at the airport at 7.00.
You didn't finish the book.
Did you watch TV yesterday? Yes, I did. No, I didn't.

topic: past simple irregular verbs: get, go, have, do
rule_en: Get, go, have, and do are irregular in the past simple (got, went, had, did). Negatives and questions still use didn't/did with the infinitive, not the irregular past form.
structure: Subject + irregular past form; negative: didn't + infinitive; question: Did + subject + infinitive?
examples_en: I got up late yesterday.
He went to work by car.
She had eggs for breakfast.
Did you get up late yesterday? Yes, I did. No, I didn't.

topic: past simple: regular and irregular verbs (review)
rule_en: Was/were is the past of am/is/are. Regular verbs add -ed or -d. Some verbs are irregular in the past simple (e.g. go -> went). Negatives of regular and irregular verbs use didn't + infinitive; questions use Did + subject + infinitive. Remember word order: ASI (Auxiliary, Subject, Infinitive) and QuASI (Question word, Auxiliary, Subject, Infinitive).
structure: be: Subject + was/were; other verbs: Subject + past form; negative: didn't + infinitive; question: Did + subject + infinitive?
examples_en: I was at home last night. I wasn't at home last night.
I played tennis yesterday. I didn't play tennis yesterday.
I got up late yesterday. I didn't get up late yesterday.
Did she want to come? What time did they get up?
